newsitem.title: UK: Unilever sees less buoyant profits growth.
newsitem.headline: Unilever sees less buoyant profits growth.

text.p: Giant Anglo-Dutch consumer group Unilever Plc/NV expects profits growth in the remainder of the year to be less buoyant, chairman Niall Fitzgerald said on Friday.
In a statement attached to the group's half-year results, he said sales growth was likely to remain modest.
"Although profits growth in the remainder of the year will be less buoyant, profit improvement for the full year will be satisfactory," said Fitzgerald.

Fitzgerald said the group did not expect economic conditions to change much in the second half of the year. The strength of sterling and the weakness of the guilder as compared to last year were likely to have a significant impact on Unilever's full-year results when expressed at current exchange rates.
Unilever announced a pre-tax profit of 4.39 billion pounds for the half year including a one-off gain of 3.02 billion from the sale of its speciality chemicals division.
Unilever completed the sale of its speciality chemicals business to Imperial Chemical Industries Plc in early July.
The sale propelled Unilever from debt into a net cash position at the half year of about 2.8 billion pounds ($4.6 billion).

Excluding profit from the sale of the chemicals business, the group's net profit rose 25 percent to 843 million over the six month period. At constant rates of exchange Unilever increased sales by three percent to 16.818 billion pounds.

The group said economic conditions were much as anticipated during the period with weakness in some key countries in mainland Europe contrasting with strong growth in many developing and emerging markets.

"Overall, margin development was once again positive, most notably in Europe. The profitability of our business increasingly reflects the benefits from cost reduction programmes and portfolio improvements," the company said. ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
